coverage_notes: Comprehensive sweep across 10 major research angles: (1) Foundational cognitive science & HCI theory (Norman on affordances/mental models, Shneiderman on direct manipulation, Tufte on visualization, Munzner's design framework, Pirolli's sensemaking); (2) Mental models specifically in AI/LLM contexts (recent CHI/arXiv 2024-2025: mental model shifts, stance attribution, multi-agent mental models, mental state attribution, co-creativity frameworks); (3) Expert/novice gaps (CHI papers, Dreyfus model, skill acquisition, metacognition); (4) Trust calibration & explainability (XAI user studies, transparency requirements, trust-reliance distinctions, trust calibration), (5) Error attribution & responsibility (stance attribution, blame games, causal responsibility); (6) Cognitive load theory and interface complexity; (7) Interaction patterns with LLMs (prompting behavior, adaptation, functional fixedness, learner interactions); (8) Visualization, sensemaking, and graph comprehension; (9) Grounding, communication, common ground in dialogue; (10) Query languages & database interfaces; plus regulatory landscape (EU AI Act, transparency requirements 2025). Deduplication: merged overlapping results (e.g., multiple citations of Norman 1988, Pirolli foundational work). Tiering: T0 sources include peer-reviewed meta-analyses, CHI/UIST proceedings, arXiv pre-prints from top venues, and current regulatory documents; T1 includes seminal author work, additional CHI/UIST papers, and high-quality NIH/Springer articles; T2 includes practitioner essays, blog summaries, and secondary analysis; T3 includes educational/glossary entries. Notable gaps: limited coverage of cross-cultural mental model differences; very limited clinical/medical AI mental model studies (found one); limited studies on mental models of different AI modalities (vision, audio, multimodal); limited longitudinal studies of mental model evolution. Reference-only licenses assigned to proprietary ACM DL paywall articles and Springer gated articles.

sources.title: The Design of Everyday Things (1988) - Norman's foundational work on mental models
sources.notes: Seminal HCI text introducing mental models concept to design; defines design model vs. user mental model vs. system image; foundational for understanding affordances and system visibility

sources.title: Affordances and Design - Don Norman's JND.org
sources.notes: Norman clarifies perceived affordances vs. real affordances; emphasizes cultural conventions and their role in user mental models; directly relevant to how users understand interface possibilities

sources.title: Common ground, cooperation, and recipient design in human-computer interactions
sources.notes: Foundation for understanding how shared mental models and common ground develop in interaction; essential for conversational grounding in AI systems

sources.title: A Functional Model of Sensemaking In a Neurocognitive Architecture - Pirolli
sources.notes: Pirolli's foundational model of sensemaking loops (foraging vs. synthesis); core theoretical framework for understanding how users construct mental models from complex information

sources.title: Information Foraging: A Theory of How People Navigate on the Web - NN/G
sources.notes: Accessible overview of Pirolli & Card's information foraging theory; explains information scent and how users' mental models guide navigation decisions

sources.title: Direct Manipulation for Comprehensible, Predictable and Controllable - Shneiderman
sources.notes: Shneiderman's principles of direct manipulation: visual presentation, rapid feedback, reversible operations; foundational for understanding how interface design shapes user mental models

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information - Edward Tufte
sources.notes: Seminal work on data visualization design; introduces chartjunk, lie factor, data-ink ratio; foundational for understanding how visualization design affects mental models of complex information

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design - Tamara Munzner
sources.notes: Comprehensive framework for visualization design (What-Why-How); theoretical foundation for understanding how visualization choices support or hinder accurate user mental models

sources.title: Mental model shifts in human-LLM interactions - Journal of Intelligent Information Systems
sources.notes: Recent empirical study (2025) documenting how user mental models of LLMs evolve through interaction; shows mental model shifts and accuracy calibration over time

sources.title: The influence of mental state attributions on trust in large language models - PMC
sources.notes: Empirical study showing how users attribute consciousness, emotions, and reasoning to LLMs; demonstrates mismatch between folk-psychological mental models and expert understanding

sources.title: Intentional or Designed? The Impact of Stance Attribution on Cognitive Processing of Generative AI Service Failures - Brain Sciences
sources.notes: Shows how users attribute failures to design vs. intent; mental models shape expectations and blame attribution in AI failure scenarios

sources.title: From Use to Oversight: How Mental Models Influence User Behavior and Output in AI Writing Assistants - CHI 2026
sources.notes: Recent CHI 2026 paper; empirical study of how different mental models of AI writing assistants affect user behavior and quality of outputs; user understanding can both help and hurt performance

sources.title: Exploring Human-AI Collaboration Using Mental Models of Early Adopters of Multi-Agent Generative AI Tools - arXiv
sources.notes: Qualitative study of 13 developers; identifies mental models of multi-agent systems (team of specialists, divide-and-conquer); transparency crucial for mental model accuracy

sources.title: An Exploration of Mental Models of AI in Human–AI Co-Creativity: A Framework and Insights - ACM TOIS
sources.notes: Framework for understanding mental models in creative AI collaboration; identifies gaps between user mental models and actual AI capabilities in creative domains

sources.title: Responsibility Attribution in Human Interactions with Everyday AI Systems - CHI 2025
sources.notes: Recent CHI 2025 empirical research on how users attribute responsibility in human-AI failure scenarios; mental models of AI autonomy shape blame attribution

sources.title: Causal Responsibility Attribution for Human-AI Collaboration - arXiv
sources.notes: Formal framework for responsibility attribution using structural causal models; addresses how user mental models of causality affect blame in collaborative AI systems

sources.title: When AI Fails, Who Do We Blame? Attributing Responsibility in Human–AI Interactions - IEEE ITTS
sources.notes: Literature review and empirical study on responsibility attribution in AI failures; demonstrates that mental models of AI intent affect blame assignment

sources.title: Expert and Novice User Differences and Implications for Product Design and Usability - Vesna Popovic
sources.notes: Classic CHI/HFES paper on expert vs. novice user differences; foundational for understanding expertise gaps in mental models and interaction strategies

sources.title: Determining Novice and Expert Status in Human–Automation Interaction Through Hidden Markov Models - HCI
sources.notes: Recent (2024) study using behavioral signatures to distinguish novice vs. expert interaction patterns with automation; shows expertise reflected in interaction strategies

sources.title: Dreyfus Model of Skill Acquisition - Wikipedia
sources.notes: Overview of Dreyfus & Dreyfus skill acquisition model; explains progression from rule-based to intuitive understanding; relevant to expert mental model differences

sources.title: Trust Calibration in AI - Emergent Mind
sources.notes: Overview of trust calibration concept; accurate mental models enable appropriate trust levels (neither over- nor under-reliance)

sources.title: Trust in AI: progress, challenges, and future directions - Nature Humanities and Social Sciences
sources.notes: Comprehensive review distinguishing trust from reliance; mental models affect both constructs differently; explains calibration problems

sources.title: Calibrating Trust, Reliance and Dependence in Variable-Reliability Automation - PMC
sources.notes: Empirical study on how user mental models track (or fail to track) actual system reliability; shows mismatches between perceived and actual automation capabilities

sources.title: Human-centered evaluation of explainable AI applications: a systematic review - PMC
sources.notes: Systematic review of XAI evaluation methodologies; shows lack of standardization in assessing whether explanations improve user mental models

sources.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) from a user perspective: A synthesis of prior literature - ScienceDirect
sources.notes: Comprehensive synthesis of XAI research from user mental model perspective; identifies how explanations are (or aren't) effective at correcting misconceptions

sources.title: From Explainable to Interactive AI: A Literature Review on Current Trends in Human-AI Interaction - arXiv
sources.notes: Recent literature review; shifts focus from one-way explanation to interactive clarification of mental models; emphasizes dialogue for grounding

sources.title: Designing AI User Interfaces That Foster Trust and Transparency - UXmatters
sources.notes: Practical design guidance for building transparent AI interfaces; emphasizes visibility of system reasoning and limitations in user mental models

sources.title: Neural Transparency: Mechanistic Interpretability Interfaces for Anticipating Model Behaviors - arXiv
sources.notes: Recent work (2025) on mechanistic interpretability interfaces; aims to surface internal model reasoning to improve user mental models of AI behavior

sources.title: "I had a solid theory before but it's falling apart": Polarizing Effects of Algorithmic Transparency - arXiv
sources.notes: Paradoxical finding: transparency can destabilize user mental models and increase cognitive load; shows explanation design matters for comprehension

sources.title: User interface design in mobile learning applications: measuring learners' extraneous cognitive load - PMC
sources.notes: Cognitive Load Theory applied to interface design; measures how interface complexity affects user ability to develop accurate mental models

sources.title: Errors + Graceful Failure - People + AI Research
sources.notes: Google PAIR framework on error recovery; shows how system feedback shapes user mental models of system capabilities and limitations

sources.title: Trapped by Expectations: Functional Fixedness in LLM-Enabled Chat Search - arXiv
sources.notes: Recent finding that users get trapped by prior mental models when using chat; prior search engine mental models interfere with effective LLM use

sources.title: Understanding Learner-LLM Chatbot Interactions and the Impact of Prompting Guidelines - arXiv
sources.notes: Study of how learners develop and refine mental models of LLM interaction through prompting guidelines; shows training improves mental model accuracy

sources.title: How understanding large language models can inform the use of ChatGPT in physics education - arXiv
sources.notes: Educational perspective on mental models of LLM capabilities; explains why users struggle and how instruction in LLM mechanics helps

sources.title: Human–LLM Interaction Patterns - Emergent Mind
sources.notes: Overview of distinctive interaction patterns between humans and LLMs; identifies how prior experience shapes interaction mental models

sources.title: Iceberg Sensemaking: A Process Model for Critical Data Analysis and Visualization - arXiv
sources.notes: Model of sensemaking through visualization; explains how visual representations support or hinder formation of mental models from complex data

sources.title: Graph visualization UX: Designing intuitive data experiences - Cambridge Intelligence
sources.notes: Best practices for graph visualization design; shows how layout, styling, and interaction affect user mental models of network relationships

sources.title: Information scent and web navigation: Theory, models and automated usability evaluation - ResearchGate
sources.notes: Applies information foraging to web navigation; shows how users' mental models of information relevance guide navigation and search

sources.title: Natural Language Interfaces for Databases: What Do Users Think? - arXiv
sources.notes: User study of NLDB mental models; shows users develop strategies for prompting databases and adapt based on feedback

sources.title: A mental model approach to teaching database querying skills with SQL and Alteryx - ScienceDirect
sources.notes: Educational research on mental models in database querying; shows how visual tools and SQL help learners develop complementary mental models

sources.title: The Role of Cognitive Biases in AI-assisted Decision-making - arXiv
sources.notes: How cognitive biases in user mental models interact with AI system design; affects over-reliance and trust calibration

sources.title: Bias in the Loop: How Humans Evaluate AI-Generated Suggestions - arXiv
sources.notes: Studies how user biases and mental models affect evaluation of AI suggestions; shows anchoring and other heuristics distort AI assessment

sources.title: AI Awareness - arXiv
sources.notes: Framework for AI metacognitive awareness; relevant to how AI systems should surface uncertainty to match user mental models

sources.title: Design Principles: Visual Perception And The Principles Of Gestalt — Smashing Magazine
sources.notes: Overview of Gestalt psychology principles; foundational for understanding how visual design shapes perception and mental model formation

sources.title: FlowForge: Guiding the Creation of Multi-agent Workflows with Design Space Visualization - arXiv
sources.notes: Visualization tool for multi-agent workflow design; shows how visual scaffolding helps users develop mental models of agent orchestration

sources.title: XAgen: An Explainability Tool for Identifying and Correcting Failures in Multi-Agent Workflows - arXiv
sources.notes: Recent tool for multi-agent explainability; addresses user mental model failures in complex agent systems; shows error propagation issues

sources.title: OrchVis: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Orchestration for Human Oversight - arXiv
sources.notes: Visualization system for human oversight of multi-agent systems; enables users to build accurate mental models of agent interactions

sources.title: Achieving Cyber Defense Situational Awareness: A Cognitive Task Analysis of Information Assurance Analysts - HFES
sources.notes: Cognitive task analysis methodology; shows how to systematically understand expert mental models and knowledge requirements in complex domains

sources.title: Individual and Distributed Cognitions in Interdisciplinary Teamwork: A Developing Case Study and Emerging Theory - Springer
sources.notes: Theory of distributed cognition across teams; shows how mental models are shared and negotiated in collaborative systems

sources.title: Pre-Act: Multi-Step Planning and Reasoning Improves Acting in LLM Agents - arXiv
sources.notes: Shows how multi-step reasoning affects LLM agent behavior and user understanding; explicit reasoning paths improve user mental models

sources.title: Levels of Autonomy for AI Agents Working Paper - arXiv
sources.notes: Framework of 5 autonomy levels (operator to observer); helps users develop appropriate mental models of agent autonomy in different contexts

sources.title: Meaningful human control: actionable properties for AI system development - AI and Ethics
sources.notes: Framework for human control in AI systems; addresses how user mental models of control should align with actual system capabilities

sources.title: Communicating uncertainty in national security intelligence: Expert and nonexpert interpretations - Risk Analysis
sources.notes: Studies how experts vs. non-experts interpret uncertainty; shows mental model differences in probability comprehension

sources.title: AI Mental Models & Trust: The Promises and Perils of Interaction Design – EPIC
sources.notes: Practitioner perspective on AI mental models and trust; emphasizes design's role in shaping user expectations

sources.title: Mental Models - People + AI Research (PAIR)
sources.notes: Google PAIR guidance on mental models; practical framework for understanding what users think AI can and can't do

sources.title: Article 13: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers - EU AI Act
sources.notes: Regulatory requirement for AI transparency; defines legal obligations for documenting AI capabilities/limitations to users

sources.title: Transparency and explainability in AI systems: global perspectives and regulation in Australia (2025) - Clayton Utz
sources.notes: Current (2025) overview of global AI transparency regulations; shows momentum toward mandated disclosure to support user mental models

sources.title: Analogy - Dedre Gentner (Cognitive Science Encyclopedia 2025)
sources.notes: Gentner's foundational work on analogy and conceptual mapping; explains how users leverage prior mental models to learn new systems

sources.title: Semantic Models for Knowledge Representation - Fraunhofer IOSB
sources.notes: Overview of semantic modeling for knowledge representation; relevant to how users represent and understand system semantics

sources.title: What Is Discoverability? — updated 2026 - IxDF
sources.notes: UX design principle; explains how interface visibility affects user discovery and mental models of available functionality

sources.title: What Are Affordances in Design? 2026 Guide & UI Examples - Parallel
sources.notes: Current (2026) guide on affordances; shows how design patterns and conventions support user mental models

sources.title: "AI enhances our performance, I have no doubt this one will do the same": The Placebo effect is robust to negative descriptions of AI - arXiv
sources.notes: Shows how user mental models (and positive expectations) affect actual performance with AI; confirms power of prior expectations

sources.title: Watching AI Think: User Perceptions of Visible Thinking in Chatbots - arXiv
sources.notes: Recent (2026) study on how showing AI reasoning (chain-of-thought) affects user mental models and trust

sources.title: When Should Users Check? A Decision-Theoretic Model of Confirmation Frequency in Multi-Step AI Agent Tasks - arXiv
sources.notes: Studies optimal user intervention points in AI agent workflows; shows users need mental models of when agent autonomy is safe

sources.title: Plan-Then-Execute: An Empirical Study of User Trust and Team Performance When Using LLM Agents As A Daily Assistant - arXiv
sources.notes: Recent study on user trust in LLM agents; shows explicit planning improves user mental models and team performance

sources.title: Teacher training in the age of AI: impact on AI literacy and teachers' attitudes (2025) - Frontiers
sources.notes: Recent evidence that training improves AI literacy and mental models; structured instruction more effective than passive exposure
